name: Main Wings
description: Wings create lift, which helps the aircraft rise and stay in the sky.

name: Tail Assembly
description: The tail helps the aircraft balance and turn more safely.

name: Jet Engine
description: The engine creates thrust so the plane can move fast enough to fly.

name: Landing Gear
description: Supports the aircraft during takeoff, landing, and taxiing.

name: Main Fuel Tank
description: Stores the fuel that powers the engine during flight.

name: Radar System
description: Helps with navigation and safer flying in difficult or rescue missions.

name: Cargo Bay
description: Lets the plane transport goods, boxes, and relief materials.

name: Passenger Seats
description: Turns a plain aircraft into a passenger-ready flight.

name: Fuselage
description: Holds the passengers, crew, and cargo together.

name: Cockpit Module
description: Houses the instruments and controls needed to fly the aircraft safely.

name: Ailerons
description: Hinged sections on the outer wings that move up and down to tilt the plane.

name: Elevators
description: Flaps on the horizontal tail that control the pitch of the airplane.

name: Rudder
description: A moving flap on the vertical tail that controls yaw (left and right).

name: Wing Flaps
description: Extend down to help the plane fly slowly during takeoff and landing.

name: Leading Edge Slats
description: Extend from the front of the wing to prevent stalling at low speeds.

name: Spoilers
description: Plates on top of the wings that pop up to reduce lift and slow down.

name: Horizontal Stabilizer
description: A mini-wing on the tail that prevents the nose from pitching up and down.

name: Vertical Stabilizer
description: The upright tail fin that stops the plane from swinging side to side.

name: Propeller System
description: Spinning blades that create thrust on certain types of aircraft.

name: Propeller Spinner
description: A cone shaped cover over the center of the propeller to improve aerodynamics.

name: Engine Nacelle
description: An aerodynamic housing that protects the engine and directs airflow.

name: Reinforced Windshield
description: Thick glass that withstands high winds and bird strikes.

name: Altimeter
description: An instrument that measures altitude using air pressure.

name: Airspeed Indicator
description: Measures the speed of the aircraft moving through the air.

name: Attitude Indicator
description: An artificial horizon that tells pilots if they are banking or climbing.

name: Control Yoke
description: The steering column pilots use to pitch and roll the plane.

name: Rudder Pedals
description: Foot pedals used to control the rudder and wheel brakes.

name: Throttle Quadrant
description: Levers pushed forward for more power and pulled back for less.

name: APU (Aux Power)
description: A small engine that generates electricity and air pressure.

name: Main Battery
description: Provides initial power to start systems and keeps critical screens running.

name: Engine Generator
description: Driven by the engines to power lights, screens, and computers.

name: Navigation Lights
description: Red, green, and white lights to show the plane's direction at night.

name: Beacon Light
description: A flashing red light that alerts ground crew to stay away.

name: Landing Lights
description: Powerful headlights used during takeoff and landing to see the runway.

name: Pitot Tube
description: A forward-facing tube that senses ram air pressure to determine speed.

name: Static Port
description: A small hole on the side of the plane to sense outside calm air pressure.

name: Transponder
description: Sends a signal to Air Traffic Control with flight number and altitude.

name: Comms Radio
description: Used to speak with Air Traffic Control and other airplanes.

name: Emergency Oxygen
description: Drops masks and supplies oxygen if the cabin loses pressure.

name: Flight Data Recorder
description: The 'black box' that saves information on speed, altitude, and controls.

name: Voice Recorder
description: Saves the audio of pilot conversations and cockpit alarms.

name: Overhead Bins
description: Compartments above the seats for carry-on luggage.

name: Galley
description: The airplane kitchen where flight attendants prepare food and drinks.

name: Lavatory
description: A small onboard bathroom with a toilet and sink.

name: Pressurization System
description: Pumps air into the cabin so people can breathe at high altitudes.

name: Environmental Control
description: Provides air conditioning and heating for the cabin.

name: Fire Extinguishers
description: Bottles of fire retardant that can be sprayed into engines or cargo holds.

name: Emergency Exits
description: Special doors and windows designed for quick evacuation.

name: Nose Radome
description: A fiberglass cover at the very front that protects the weather radar.

name: Trim Tabs
description: Small flaps on control surfaces that relieve steering pressure for the pilot.
